thread.title: If S&P 500 Doesn't Blow Past This Key Value, Look Out Below

author: Home
title: If S&P 500 Doesn't Blow Past This Key Value, Look Out Below
text:
It's time for stocks to flex their muscles. If not, then a vicious selloff may be in the cards.
Or so says the stock chart watchers. Points out Bank of America Merrill Lynch's technical strategist Stephen Suttmeier:
"Neither the bulls nor bears have taken control but as highlighted above the trend is up (aka rising 200-day MA) and the indicator weight of the evidence supports the bull case. Last week's low near 2611 coincides with the rising 200-day MA and is key support above the early April/early February lows at 2553-2532. The mid April peak near 2718 is key resistance ahead of 2741-2750 (3/22 downside gap) and 2789-2802 (late Feb/mid Mar peaks). If the bulls cannot take charge given a positive indicator weight of the evidence and break 2718 resistance, we cannot rule out an undercut to 2469-2462 given the February to March rising or bearish wedge completed on March 19."
Since you probably have no clue what a bearish wedge is, just remember that the February lows could be in play if upward momentum doesn't return to the S&P 500 and push it toward 2,718. A burst higher could easily happen in the short-term should market leader Apple ( AAPL ) manage to trounce Wall Street profit estimates on Tuesday.
Apple is holding in Jim Cramer's Action Alerts PLUS .
Tweetable Stat:
The S&P 500 has tested its rising 200-day moving average three times during the correction off the late January peak of 2872.87, says BofA.
Stocks need to flex their muscles, or else. Source: BofA.
